what.distroHint: CaffeineOS, CoffinOS, AmiKit or an ART Baseline, with the system already installed.

prepare.heading: Prepare the card
prepare.explain: Writing the image, adapting it to your PiStorm through the hardware settings ART already knows, placing your Kickstart, creating the multiboot set and verifying the result. None of it is built yet.

licence.freeGrey: {{name}} is given away free by the people who make it, and carries AmigaOS material they cannot license. ART does not police your copy and does not fetch it either.
licence.userLicensed: {{name}} is a commercial product built on an AmigaOS you must own. ART prepares the card their product expects; it does not reproduce their work.
licence.artBaseline: Built by ART from your own licensed media. Shareable as a recipe — never as an image.

supply.card: A card of at least {{gb}} GB.

image.tooSmallForRaw: {{gb}} GB is far too small to be a {{name}} image — this is probably the wrong file, or a download that stopped early.

caffeineos.download: Distributed as a single raw image of about 17 GB. Written with any imager; ART will adapt it to your hardware once that step exists.
caffeineos.network: CaffeineOS runs its own networking stack (Miami DX with wifipi.device), not the Roadshow one — so WiFi is changed with its own tool on the Amiga, not by editing DEVS:NetInterfaces. Whichever stack a system uses, the settings live on the Amiga side and not in the boot files.

coffinos.romFamily: CoffinOS states that Hyperion's 3.1.4 and 3.2 Kickstarts break it. It wants a classic 3.1 ROM.
coffinos.demoware: Ships demo versions of Roadshow and iBrowse.

amikit.ownIt: AmiKit is a commercial product. You supply your own AmigaOS 3.2 and P96; they ship only their own layer.
amikit.adaptOnly: ART prepares the card their product expects. It does not rebuild AmiKit.

baseline.recipe: ART builds this from your media and can share how it was built — the recipe, not the result.
baseline.yourMedia: Nothing is bundled. Your OS, your ROM, your licences.
baseline.boingBags: BoingBag 1 and 2 were always free downloads and ART can fetch them on request.
baseline.romFamily: A 3.9 system wants a classic 3.1 ROM, not a Hyperion 3.1.4 or 3.2 one.

pistorm.title: PiStorm & Emu68 Card
pistorm.intro: Every control here writes a documented Emu68 option or a Raspberry Pi firmware setting — and shows you which one. Both files are merged into what is already on the card, never rewritten.

hardware.heading: Hardware
hardware.intro: Three answers, because what a setup can do depends on all three: the kernel follows the board, the storage driver's name follows the Pi, and which options apply at all follows the Amiga.

note.pi-not-guaranteed: This Pi is reported working on this board by users, but the project does not guarantee it.
note.cm4-needs-lite-for-sd-card: A Compute Module 4 with onboard eMMC cannot use the microSD slot at the same time. The usual recommendation is a CM4 Lite with no eMMC.
note.pi-physical-fit: A 3B or 3B+ needs its ports removed, or a taller stacking header, to fit this board. A Zero 2 W or 3A+ fits as it is.
note.no-activity-led: The 3B has no activity-LED support here.
note.needs-cpu-adapter: This machine needs a CPU adapter to take the board.
note.power-supply-quality: Use a good power supply. If the 5 V rail sags the Pi quietly underclocks itself, which looks exactly like a slow PiStorm and is the commonest cause of one.
note.ram-beyond-what-amiga-os-uses: AmigaOS does not use more than 2 GB of Fast RAM, so a Pi with more is not buying the Amiga anything.

card.heading: The card
card.needed: Everything on this screen edits files on a card. Choose its boot folder — the FAT32 partition of a card you have written, or a folder you are assembling one in — and the rest becomes available.

card.kickstartsMissing: No Kickstart image found on the card.
card.kernelUnknownVersion: Emu68.img is on the card, but it does not state a version.

scan.notACard: {{path}} has no Emu68 kernel and no config.txt, so it does not look like a PiStorm card yet.

profiles.heading: Ready-made settings
profiles.intro: Each one is a set of Emu68 options, listed under it. Applying a profile replaces the options; nothing else on the card changes until you save.

profile.applied: {{name}} applied. Nothing is written until you save.

performance.title: Performance
performance.description: The fastest Workbench and RTG, for work where exact timing does not matter.

daily.title: Everyday & WHDLoad
daily.description: Balanced defaults. WHDLoad runs in NOMMU mode — Emu68 emulates no MMU, so there is no other mode to run in.

compatibility.title: Compatibility & demoscene
compatibility.description: Closer to the original bus timing: accuracy instead of speed. On an A500-family machine this also moves the trapdoor memory to CHIP.

diagnostics.title: Diagnostics
diagnostics.description: For hunting a problem, not for using the machine. Verbose logging slows everything down.

display.heading: Display & clock
display.auto: Let the firmware ask the monitor
display.customHint: a pair the presets do not cover

overclock.enable: Run the Pi faster than it is sold to run
overclock.warning: Heat, and the quality of your power supply. On a Raspberry Pi this sets the warranty bit. Never part of a profile — only ever something you turn on yourself.

advanced.heading: Every option
advanced.intro: The full Emu68 inventory, each row labelled with the token it writes. Options that mean nothing on the hardware above are not shown.

option.storage_unit0: how the Amiga sees the card
option.storage_verbose: how much the storage driver logs (0–2)
option.storage_low_speed: stay off the 50 MHz mode, for a card that will not take it
option.z2_ram_size: Zorro II RAM in MB (0, 1, 2, 4 or 8)
option.copy_rom_kb: copy ROM into fast RAM, in KB
option.vc4_mem_mb: video memory reported to Picasso96, in MB
option.swap_df0_with: swap DF0 with another drive (1, 2 or 3)
option.buptest_kb: memory test at startup, in KB

saved.withBackup: Saved. The previous version is at {{path}}.

wifi.heading: WiFi & network
wifi.explain: WiFi on a PiStorm is an Amiga-side matter, not a boot option: wifipi.device with Roadshow, configured in DEVS:NetInterfaces on the system volume. It belongs to building the volumes, which ART cannot do yet.

sets.intro: One config.txt per system, copied over the active one to choose which boots — the pattern MultibootOS uses. ART does not read what is inside them.

preload.heading: Prepare the card's Amiga volumes
preload.intro: A card ART builds has partitions an Amiga can see and nothing inside them — the Amiga offers to format them on first boot. This formats them here instead, and copies your content in, so the card arrives ready.
preload.scope: ART writes PFS3 and FFS itself by default, through its own writer — no external tool needed for an ordinary card. hst-imager, the same tool both existing PiStorm imagers stand on, stays as a named fallback for the two things ART's own writer cannot yet do: embedding a driver into a card's existing RDB in place, and an AmigaDOS name outside plain ASCII on a PFS3 volume. Set your own copy of it if either applies to this card.

pairing.unsuitable: This system was built for a Kickstart V{{needs}} or newer, and the card carries {{rom}}, which states V{{found}}. The Amiga will start and stop asking for a newer ROM. Preparing the card anyway is fine — the ROM can be replaced afterwards without rebuilding anything.
pairing.unsuitable47: This system was built for a Kickstart V{{needs}} or newer, and the card carries {{rom}}, which states V{{found}}. The Amiga will start and stop with "This disk must be booted from Kickstart ROM 3.2 (V47) or from the 'Modules' disk that matches your hardware." Preparing the card anyway is fine — the ROM can be replaced afterwards without rebuilding anything.
pairing.unsuitableUnknown: This system was built for a Kickstart V{{needs}} or newer, and {{rom}} on the card states no version at all, so ART cannot tell whether it will run. The Amiga may stop asking for a newer ROM.

reason.conditionOff: Off — the paired Kickstart is {{rom}}, at or above V{{major}}, so this release's own Startup-Sequence does not need it. You can still switch it on yourself.

confirmOff.warning: This ROM is below V{{major}}. This release's own Startup-Sequence quits without these files — turning them off means the system will not boot. It is your machine to decide.

packages.intro: Add an official update — a BoingBag, or an unofficial pack like the Turkish catalogs — onto a distribution tree ART, or you, already built.
packages.scopeNote: ART ships a recipe for {{count}} update packages — each one a hand-written list of files and their own destinations — and will touch no other archive. A package with no such recipe, or one whose own installer is an Amiga Installer script deciding what to do at run time on real hardware, cannot be placed here: there is nothing for ART to reproduce that decision with.
packages.scopeBlocked: {{count}} of them cannot be placed from Windows at all, however many copies of the archive you have — each says why on its own row below.

blocked.encryptedPayload: The files inside this package are locked, and only the package's own Amiga-side Updater has the key. That Updater is an Amiga program: it has to run on the Amiga itself, which is how every other distribution builder installs this package too. ART will not break the lock, so it cannot place a single file from here — put the archive on your Amiga and run its own Updater there instead.
blocked.chosen: {{names}} cannot be placed from Windows, so nothing can be previewed or added for this selection. Untick it, or add it on the Amiga with the package's own Updater.

packages.refusedNames: This archive carries {{count}} entry name(s) ART refuses to use, because they point outside the folder they belong in: {{names}}. Nothing will ever be placed from them — the rest of the archive is unaffected.
packages.archiveGone: This package stays ticked because you chose it, but its archive is no longer in the update packages folder — nothing will be added for it. Untick it, or put the archive back and it will be offered again.
packages.unknownHint: This id was remembered from an earlier choice, but it is not one of the packages ART ships today — a stale pick, most likely from an older version. Untick it; nothing will be added for it either way.
packages.needsFolderToPreview: Choose the update packages folder above to preview what these {{count}} package(s) would replace.

preview.heading: {{downgrades}} downgrades, {{upgrades}} upgrades, {{sameVersion}} same version, {{unversioned}} unversioned
preview.nothing: Nothing on the tree would be replaced.

packages.undeclared: Undeclared — this package's own recipe never said it may replace this file
packages.confirm: I confirm this set of {{count}} package(s) will replace the files listed above.

amigaInstall.heading: Run a package's own installer on the Amiga
amigaInstall.intro: Some update packages cannot be placed from Windows at all: the files inside them are locked, and only the package's own Amiga program has the key. ART does not break that lock. It copies your distribution tree, starts an emulator, and lets the package install itself — which is how every established Amiga distribution builder installs these packages too.
amigaInstall.chainNote: These go on in order: a clean AmigaOS 3.9, then BoingBag 3.9-1, then BoingBag 3.9-2, and only then the community BoingBag 3 and 4. ART reads the tree's own record before it copies anything, so a package whose predecessor is missing is refused first and told which one to install, in which order.
amigaInstall.emulatorWindow: This opens a real emulator window on this desktop and drives it. Leave it alone while it works — closing that window ends the run before the installer has said anything.
amigaInstall.copyNote: The install runs against a copy of your tree, never the tree itself. The copy replaces it only when the installer reports success; if it does not, your tree is left exactly as it was and this screen says where the copy is.

package.label: Package
package.needsFolder: Choose the update packages folder above to see which packages ART can run on the Amiga.
package.none: None of the packages ART ships carries an installer it can run on the Amiga.
package.unavailableHint: ART could not read the shipped package list.

archive.label: The package's own archive
archive.chooseTitle: Choose the package's own archive — the file you downloaded
archive.hint: The archive as you downloaded it, e.g. BoingBag39-1.lha. ART unpacks it and mounts it as its own Amiga volume; the locked part inside stays locked and is handed to the package's own installer.

overlayArchive.label: The package's update archive (only if it needs one)
overlayArchive.hint: A second archive that replaces part of the first — the fix some packages shipped separately for their own installer. Leave it empty unless the note below asks for it.

kickstart.label: Your own Kickstart ROM
kickstart.chooseTitle: Choose your own licensed Kickstart ROM
kickstart.hint: The emulator boots the tree with this. ART ships no Kickstart and never will — it has to be your own.

preview.heading: What will run
preview.needsChoices: Choose a distribution tree, a package, its own archive and your Kickstart, and this will say exactly what would run.
preview.deadline: If nothing answers within {{minutes}} minutes, ART ends the emulator it started and reports that nobody answered — it never leaves a run waiting for ever.
preview.volumes: The Amiga will see {{system}}: (your tree), {{package}}: (the package, unpacked) and {{work}}: (ART's own boot volume, which carries the script and nothing of yours).
preview.resultFile: The Amiga writes {{file}} on ART's volume and ART reads it back; that file is the installer's own answer, not ART's opinion of it.

overlay.needed: This package's installer has to state at least {{version}} to work inside an emulator, and the build inside the original download is older than that. If yours is that build, ART refuses the run and copies nothing. The fix is one more download — the package's own update archive, the one carrying {{overlays}}. Choose it as the second archive above and ART copies it over the package's drawer before the run.
overlay.supplied: ART will copy {{overlays}} out of your second archive over the package's own drawer before the run, so the installer that runs is at least {{version}} — the build that works inside an emulator.

blocker.heading: Not ready to run yet
blocker.archiveMissing_one: The archive chosen above is not there any more. ART checked the {{count}} file you chose.
blocker.archiveMissing_other: One of the archives chosen above is not there any more. ART checked all {{count}} files you chose.
blocker.noEmulator: No emulator was found. Set WinUAE's path in Settings — ART starts an emulator you already have, it does not install one.

refused.heading: ART will not run this
refused.nothingCopied: Nothing has been copied and your own tree has not been touched. The sentence above is ART's own and is written in English whatever language you chose.

amigaInstall.confirm: I understand: an emulator window will open on this desktop, and my tree is replaced only if the installer itself reports success.
amigaInstall.run: Run the installer on the Amiga
amigaInstall.cancelled: The run was cancelled. The copy has been discarded and your own tree is untouched.

outcome.succeeded: The package's own installer reported success.
outcome.failed: The installer ran and said no — it reported a failure of its own.
outcome.timedOut: Nobody answered. The installer was still waiting {{seconds}} seconds in, so ART ended the emulator it had started.
outcome.emulatorClosed: The emulator window was closed {{seconds}} seconds in, before the installer had reported anything.

next.succeeded: Boot the tree and ask the running system what it is — the version it states about itself, not a copyright line on a screen.
next.failed: Look inside the copy: whatever the installer wrote is there, and its own messages are what say why it refused.
next.timedOut: Run it again and watch the emulator window this time. An Amiga installer asks questions, and this one was waiting for an answer nobody gave it.
next.emulatorClosed: Run it again and let the window finish. ART cannot say what the installer would have done, so nothing was decided either way.

settlement.promoted: Your tree at {{tree}} is the installed one now.
settlement.promotedLeftBehind: Your tree at {{tree}} is the installed one now. The tree it replaced could not be deleted — something still has it open — and is sitting at {{leftBehind}}; it is yours to remove when you want to.
settlement.kept: Your own tree at {{original}} was not touched. The copy the installer worked on is at {{copy}}, kept exactly as it was left, so you can look at what happened.

replaces.heading: What this would replace
replaces.summary: {{components}} would place {{placed}} files: {{fresh}} new, {{unchanged}} already identical, and {{replaced}} over files another part of this release puts down first.
